outcome.technical: tools/capture-screenshots.mjs plus nine cases in tools/ui-tests/capture-provenance.test.mjs. PROBE (host en_US@rg=rszzzz, 2026-10-17): a bare date input renders 'dd. mm. yyyy.' under --lang=en-US; none of these moved it: --lang=en/en_US/en-GB/en-US-u-rg-uszzzz/--accept-lang, LC_ALL/LANG/LANGUAGE, CFFIXED_USER_HOME with and without __CFPREFERENCES_AVOID_DAEMON, '-AppleLocale en_US[@rg=uszzzz]' on the browser argv via a wrapper executable, element lang; only non-English --lang changed it (de-DE, es-US). Cause shown with osascript: NSDateFormatter yMd over NSLocale.currentLocale = 'd. M. y.', over explicit en_US = 'M/d/y'. So the placeholder cannot be pinned and is READ instead. Added: readRegionalFormat() (osascript/NSLocale, darwin only, failure returned as error), pure exported regionalFormatProblem/regionalFormatBasis/dateInputProblem, visibleDateInputs() (uses checkVisibility(): a rect test alone counted a closed <details> input, caught by my in-run proof), assertDateInputCheckWorks() run by --check on every host, shot() refusal in the writing path for a shot holding a visible native date input on a differing/unreadable host, --accept-host-date-format as the explicit recorded way past (also what --repro passes), sidecar entry nativeDateInput {regionalFormat[, hostFormatAccepted]}, machineFingerprint()/--repro line 'host regional format', a --check note naming the 8 report shots affected. Evidence: refusal run (--only report --out scratch, exit 1, 8 refused, nothing written); accept run exit 0, sidecar records en_US@rg=rszzzz + hostFormatAccepted; fake-osascript clean host: exit 0, no refusal, sidecar 'en_US'; fake osascript exit 1: exit 1 'could not be read'; mutations M1 (count ignored) 1 red, M2 (compare inverted) 4 red, M3 (error as clean) 1 red, all restored byte-identical; node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check exit 0 on the second run (first run exit 1 on 'gate card: an event appended ... never reached the Overview table within 6.5s', unrelated to this change, not reproduced); --repro --only report exit 0 and prints the regional line; npx vitest run: 56 files, 839 passed; python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet exit 0 (335/335 files). Not run: tools/verify.sh (forbidden), the committed screenshots were NOT regenerated and captured-at.json NOT touched (existing entries lack nativeDateInput until the next capture).
outcome.descriptive: A capture that would write PNGs with host-shaped date inputs now refuses (or, with --accept-host-date-format, writes and records the acceptance), and --check and --repro print the host regional format, instead of the limit living only in a comment.
